title: 226. summertime sadness?! answering your most asked mental health q’s
description_html:
in this week’s solo episode, i’m answering a question on so many of your minds right now: why can summer be so hard on our mental health?!

here, i’ll be sharing my favorite psychology insights on why our mental health can struggle in the summer before reacting to trending tiktoks, articles, and reddit posts on summer mental health. i wrap things up by explaining how you can set yourself up for success this summer (and in summers to come!).
talk_about: a mental health mantra you need to hear
making your environment work for your mental health
my theory on why mental health can decline in the summer
why school is actually good for mental health (shocking, i know)
finding purpose + structure during summer break
how to stay social + make friends in summer
battling boredom + loneliness when you’re home for the summer
choosing the right summer job for you
the importance of actually relaxing during summer
life hacks for getting out of a mental health rut

summary: sadie explores why summer can be surprisingly hard on mental health, even though we expect it to be relaxing. she explains how school acts as a built-in protective system—providing structure, social connection, purpose, and routine—and how losing that over summer makes us emotionally vulnerable. through reddit posts and tiktoks from listeners struggling with summer sadness, loneliness, and lack of motivation, she breaks down why we can't just rely on willpower to feel better. her main advice: create external systems (jobs with social coworkers, set plans with friends, hobbies with built-in accountability) instead of setting goals you have to force yourself to meet. she also reassures listeners that needing less socializing in summer might be okay, and that rest isn't lazy if you genuinely feel fine.
quote: we don't rise to our goals, we fall to the level of our systems.
